items.title: Gemini and the path to AGI with Koray Kavukcuoglu
items.summary: Seven years after their last conversation at Google DeepMind’s London office, Professor Hannah Fry reunites with Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect at Google. items.title: He Used 100 Billion Tokens in a Month - Waymo Talks
items.summary: What happens when your AI coding agent gets better at finding bugs - but never knows when to stop? Jesse Vincent, creator of Superpowers and founder of Prime Radiant, joins us to explore what it actually takes to get useful work out of AI agents. We start with a tiny Playdate game console turned into a voice-controlled client for his coding agent. Then we dig into why agents ignore skills, what goes wrong when code review becomes an endless loop, and Jesse’s experience using 100 billion tokens in a month - including turning 30 years of email into a searchable personal knowledge base. Jesse also walks through his custom coding agent, Evener, his approach to preserving context, and why asking an agent for a video proving its work can reveal what tests miss. Finally, we explore AI colleagues with ongoing jobs: project managers and developers that coordinate work, ship fixes, and run postmortems. If you use Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, or other AI coding tools, this conversation offers practical ideas for moving from generated code to software you can actually ship. items.summary: Michael Tomasello is a developmental psychologist who spent twenty years at the Max Planck Institute in Germany putting children and great apes into the same experiments, and is now back at Duke University. His book The Evolution of Agency asks what it takes for a living thing, or a machine, to act for its own reasons. SPONSOR: --- Cyber Fund built the Monastery to help founders ship products that were impossible a year ago. Apply now: https://cyber.fund --- His answer starts with unpredictability. Where the environment is predictable, nature builds the behaviour in; where it isn't, it builds a decision maker. Tim and Tomasello test that on a dumb traffic light, a thermostat and a robot vacuum, then follow the line to humans: reptiles running simple control loops, a squirrel that imagines itself falling and takes another branch, and great apes that go looking for more information before they commit. The second half is about shared agency. Humans form joint goals, attend to the same things together, and learn that one object can be seen from different perspectives. Children who lose the sound on a video call invent gestures and turn them into conventions. Large language models, Tomasello argues, started at the endpoint and skipped that infrastructure. items.title: NLP Prediction, Vision Modeling & Clustering: AI Across Data Types
items.summary: Machine learning is not limited to numbers in a spreadsheet. Text, images and unlabeled data all carry patterns a model can learn from. Terms covered: - NLP Prediction: making predictions from text rather than generating it. Routing support tickets by urgency, classifying sentiment in financial news, flagging patients at elevated risk from clinical notes. - Vision Modeling: the same principle applied to images and video. Detecting production line defects in milliseconds, identifying anomalies in medical scans, tracking infrastructure change from satellite imagery. - Clustering: finding natural groupings based on similarity with no predefined categories. The model does not classify, it discovers. Text, images and unlabeled data. Three very different inputs, made meaningful through the same underlying capability. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #MachineLearning #ComputerVision #Clustering #AIGlossary #H2Oai
